title: Camera-site tier 1g ('shared upstream ref') compares bare normalised ref strings with no id namespace and no per-capture uniqueness check, so equal row numbers or OBJECTIDs from unrelated layers qualify for auto-write; a 1g match is not evidence of a shared upstream record
evidence: normalize_ref() only trims, lower-cases and strips a trailing '.0' (camera_sites.py:306-318); tier 1 = ref_equal (normalize_ref(a.external_ref) == normalize_ref(b.external_ref)) plus mutual-nearest and co-location/name rules within candidate_max_m 50 m (camera_sites.py:837-873); no field records which id namespace a ref belongs to, and refs fall back to server row ids (OBJECTID/FID; L1 NEW-3) that L2 NEW-1 shows are non-unique within layers (IL DOT 2,936 of 3,000 subjects collided); the rules file itself notes 'a shared row number' cannot disambiguate co-located devices (camera_site_rules.toml:48-54); tier 1g is in candidate_auto_write=[1,3] and auto-wrote 1,089 decisions in the recorded P30.2b run (F-257); inference=two unrelated layers numbering rows 1..N can produce a same-number pair within 50 m that passes as 1g; why=an auto-write tier whose basis is not a shared upstream record cannot be census-verified; L3 requires a declared id_namespace (tier C1) and routes namespace-less 1g pairs to possible-duplicate

title: The spec has no boundary between derivation (records that are copies of one upstream record, SIG-EPIS-009) and identity inference (independent records judged to be one physical device): SIG-IDENT-020 lets tiers 0-3 auto-write while SIG-EVAL-004 requires a human-labelled >=0.98 lower bound 'for each authorized tier', and no text or ADR says which governs identifier- or lineage-based merges
evidence: spec:2467-2479 SIG-IDENT-020 table: tier 0 'exact shared canonical identifier' and tier 1 'exact upstream-id crosswalk already established' -> Auto-write; spec:7325 SIG-EVAL-004: 'Auto-write eligibility must use a preregistered lower confidence bound of at least 0.98 on strict precision for each authorized tier'; spec:1449 SIG-EPIS-029 and SIG-EPIS-009 treat republication as derivation to be declared; ADR-105 maps camera tiers 1g/3g onto spec tiers 1/3 and gates both on an agent-verified holdout, mixing mirror copies (95 of 180 holdout pairs, L1) with independent-source coincidence; why=under U-008 (no independent humans) the only honest auto-write is a mechanically verifiable copy-collapse, which needs this boundary written down; L3 proposes SIG-CONF-D04/D05 and records EVAL-004 as WAIVED(ADR-L3-B) scoped to C0-C2 rather than re-reading the clause

title: The G3 promotion gate is all-or-nothing ('any failure or skip blocks promotion; a waiver only with Class S') while 29 of L2's 45 graph-quality metrics fail today, so adopting the L1/L2 invariants as V-checks would block every release or force per-release waivers; a ratchet mode (baseline + no-regression, flipped to enforce by the fixing ticket) is missing from both designs
evidence: G3 §5.5: 'Any failure or skip blocks promotion; a waiver is possible only with Class S and is recorded in the readout'; status census of data/l2_metrics.csv (python csv Counter, this row): fail 29, warn 11, ok 5; L1 §6.2 marks 13 of its 17 invariants 'fails' or 'expected to fail' today; B4 G10 places probes but defines no ratchet; why=without a ratchet the suite is either report-only (does not hold fixes) or blocking (no release ships), and routine waivers would train the operator to sign past red checks; L3 ADR-L3-C and SIG-CONF-D07 add the ratchet, analogous to the repo's LD- xfail convention

title: Same-layer co-located distinct records (multi-view camera sites published as one row per view) are counted as duplicates and anomalies by L2's exact-coordinate duplicate share and per-source anomaly rate (e.g. IA DOT 99.2%); checks must separate 'multi-view' from 'copy' before any duplicate threshold applies
evidence: L2-M01 counts same-source exact-coordinate points as duplicates (same-source 0.1064 of 0.1185); L2-M42 lists IA DOT at 99.2% anomaly rate from 'exact-coordinate pairs'; L2 §5 already notes distance-based duplicates 'include legitimate co-located multi-camera mounts' but the metric and the proposed C3/C4 checks do not classify them; ADR-105 records 36,437 same-source pairs within 1 m explained as 'poles and intersections carrying several cameras'; inference=DOT layers commonly publish one row per camera view at one site with distinct ids; to verify in CONF-01 (compare ids, names and directions within same-layer coordinate groups); why=a duplicate check that flags multi-view sites would push fixes toward merging distinct devices, the opposite of the conservative direction
